transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Jordan Li (Redwood SE); Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM); Olivia Martinez (Radiant Head of Eng); Dr. Samir Rao (Radiant CTO); Priya Nair (Radiant Data Eng Manager); Alex Gomez (Radiant Security)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — really excited to kick off with Radiant. Quick round-robin and then we can go through goals.
[00:07] Olivia (Radiant): Hi yes thanks, Olivia here. We run the platform team at Radiant, looking forward to getting this moving.
[00:11] Samir (Radiant CTO): Samir here, will be involved in architecture and security decisions.
[00:15] Maya: Awesome. Jordan, want to do a quick intro on the technical side?
[00:18] Jordan (Redwood SE): Yeah hi all — Jordan, solutions. I'll be your technical lead for the pilot and run the initial benchmarks. We'll focus on latency, throughput, and cost per token for typical Radiant queries.
[00:28] Ravi (Redwood CSM): And I'm Ravi, I'll coordinate success criteria and weekly touchpoints.
[00:33] Priya (Radiant): Priya here; I'll own data shipping and sample datasets.
[00:36] Alex (Radiant Security): Alex — security and compliance. I'll be tracking SOC 2, KMS, and SSO requirements.

[02:00] Maya: Great. Playbook overview — our onboarding usually has three phases: discovery & pilot scoping, pilot execution (benchmarks, evals), and rollout (canary -> production). For most customers we start on hosted to get quick results, then evaluate Dedicated or Private if they need VPC or strict data controls.
[02:25] Olivia: Our priority is patient-data privacy and latency. We need sub-200ms 95th percentile on the most common user flows. Cost is important but less so than reliability. Timeline: we'd like to be live with a pilot within 6 weeks.
[02:45] Maya: Good, 6 weeks is doable. Two questions: will you need private deployment/VPC from day one, or can we start hosted with guaranteed data handling?
[03:00] Samir: We'd prefer private VPC eventually, but for the pilot we can start hosted if data residency and encryption are covered. We need audit logs and customer-managed KMS ideally.
[03:18] Jordan: That's fine — hosted plus customer KMS is common. One thing to watch is model variants and quantization: Dedicated gives more control over quant profiles and lower per-token cost for heavy workloads.
[03:34] Priya: Also want to know about data retention and delete policies — can you confirm log retention defaults?
[03:40] Ravi: By default hosted API retains logs for 30 days, but for enterprise we have options for extended retention or no retention depending on contract. We'll share a security doc.

[05:00] Jordan: For benchmarking, can you share 5 representative calls and a 1GB-ish sample? That lets us profile sequence lengths and KV cache usage.
[05:12] Priya: Yep we can do that. We'll anonymize and send.
[05:16] Alex: We need to review your SOC 2 report and pen test summaries. Also confirm SSO — we use Okta.
[05:25] Maya: Okta is supported; we'll send the SSO SAML setup guide. We'll also send SOC 2 and data flow diagram.

[07:10] Olivia: On the pilot scope — what does success look like from your perspective?
[07:15] Ravi: We'll help you define measurable criteria — typical examples: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for critical path, error rate < 0.5% under expected load, and cost per active session under a threshold. We'll tailor it to Radiant's traffic shape.
[07:33] Samir: We also want to validate that model outputs meet clinical tolerances — hallucination checks and safety filters.
[07:42] Jordan: We can set up an eval harness to track quality regressions across model versions and quantized variants. Redwood Optimize will flag regressions.

[09:05] Maya: Budget/contract side — do you have a procurement timeline?
[09:12] Olivia: We'll do an internal approval in 2-3 weeks. The pilot likely goes through procurement for Dedicated if we decide to reserve.
[09:20] Maya: Great. We'll send pricing lanes for Hosted vs Dedicated for the expected load.

[11:00] Jordan: Technical note: if you plan private deployment (VPC/on-prem), we'll need a tech deep-dive to discuss networking, peering, and HSM/KMS integrations. That usually adds 2 weeks to setup.
[11:18] Samir: Understood. For HSM, we prefer customer-managed keys in cloud KMS.
[11:25] Jordan: We support both customer KMS (bring-your-own) and Redwood-managed keys; we'll document tradeoffs.

[12:50] Priya: For integrations, we use a microservice layer — we'll probably call Redwood via REST as a single endpoint. Any SDK preferences?
[12:58] Jordan: REST is fine; we have SDKs for Node/Python but many customers integrate via REST. We'll share quickstart snippets. Also note streaming vs non-streaming affects latency; streaming may add small overhead but improves perceived latency on long responses.

[15:00] Olivia: Competitors — we've evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic in the past. Can you highlight what Redwood gives us operationally?
[15:10] Maya: Sure — our differentiator is production-first controls: consistent runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, transparent latency/cost dashboards, and fallbacks so your app stays up if a model variant is slow. We also provide rollout controls and canarying.
[15:30] Samir: On the model side — do you manage the models or do we pick open models?
[15:36] Jordan: We host curated open models and can onboard custom models; we also provide quantization profiles that balance cost and quality. For clinical use we'll recommend models with guardrails and run evals against your prompt sets.

[18:00] Olivia: For the pilot, is it reasonable to start with hosted but with the expectation we'll move to Dedicated if performance needs it?
[18:08] Maya: Yes that's the usual path. Start hosted to iterate quickly, then switch to Dedicated or Private for production. We can provision Dedicated capacity for the pilot period if you prefer to test under reserved throughput.
[18:25] Priya: Cost estimate request: can you give an example monthly cost for X qps and Y tokens?
[18:30] Maya: We'll send a spreadsheet with sample calculations — Jordan will run the benchmark to fill in actual token breakdowns.

[21:00] Jordan: Quick technical caveat: KV cache hit rates and batching behavior significantly affect per-token latency and cost. We'll instrument to show where batching helps and recommend a cache TTL.
[21:15] Priya: Good to know. We'll include typical request patterns in the sample.

[23:40] Alex: Regarding compliance, will audit logs be exportable to our SIEM?
[23:46] Ravi: Yes, we support log exports and can integrate with common SIEMs or push logs to a customer S3 with encryption. We'll include options in the security pack.

[26:00] Maya: Let's confirm immediate next steps: 1) Redwood sends onboarding plan, security docs, SSO setup guide, and pricing spreadsheet. 2) Radiant shares sample requests and anonymized sample dataset and confirms KMS preference. 3) Schedule technical deep-dive the week of 3/23 with Jordan.
[26:25] Olivia: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the sample dataset by 3/23.

[28:00] Jordan: Any blockers we should know now?
[28:05] Samir: Mainly procurement review and legal — would like to see SLAs and data handling terms.
[28:12] Maya: We'll include a standard enterprise SLA and options for extended retention and higher uptime in the materials.

[33:00] Priya: Small transcription note — when you say KV cache, sometimes internal folks misread it. We call it the context cache.
[33:10] Jordan: Totally — I'll call it context/KV cache in docs.

[35:00] Olivia: Can you also share example rollout plan and canary metrics?
[35:06] Ravi: Yes — we'll share a typical canary checklist: traffic % ramp, error and latency thresholds, rollback triggers, and monitoring dashboards.

[38:00] Maya: Great. Any final questions?
[38:05] Alex: Just to confirm — SSO Okta, customer KMS preferred, SOC 2 report required.
[38:12] Maya: Got it — we'll prioritize those in the security pack.

[40:00] Olivia: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity. We'll review materials and confirm the tech deep-dive slot.
[40:07] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and the onboarding plan by 3/20.
[40:12] Jordan: I'll request the sample dataset and then run an initial hosted benchmark once we have it.
[40:20] Ravi: I'll send calendar invites for weekly check-ins.

[44:00] Maya: Ok thanks all, talk soon.
[44:05] Samir: Thanks.

Notes: deck link shared in chat: https://redwood.ai/welcome-deck (placeholder). Security docs to be shared via secure link. Some minor transcription artifacts (names/titles may be slightly mis-typed).
